literature_frameworks.implication: Scent can shape abstract quality and sophistication cues, and service environments often benefit more from scent than plain retail.
Breadth can help extension confidence, but excess complexity can create overload if the brand does not simplify decision making.
Premium-attainable brands can scale through accessibility, but wider availability can weaken distinctiveness if scarcity and symbolic value erode.
Coherent visual cues support premiumness, and rarity tends to create stronger value than exclusivity theater alone.

brand_architecture.justification: MITH has a clearer mass-premium consumer house architecture, while VIBES LAB has a sharper scent-as-memory plus scent-branding architecture. Both are coherent, but they are coherent in different business shapes.

MITH Bangkok.justification: Made-in-Thailand and friendship language gives the brand a local identity anchor, but the consumer house story is broader than it is singular.

VIBES LAB.justification: Aromachology, memory, and scent-branding create a distinctive architecture, though the DTC perfume line and B2B platform can blur into two offers for some shoppers.

product_portfolio.justification: Both brands sell perfume, but MITH has a materially broader product map across fragrance, home scent, and body-adjacent categories at much higher SKU count.

MITH Bangkok.justification: 161 listed products and category spread from perfume to home fragrance, body care, and inhalers indicate strong assortment depth.

VIBES LAB.justification: The assortment is curated and coherent, but 13 perfumes plus a few home-scent categories is a smaller offer than MITH's breadth play.

olfactory_positioning.justification: MITH covers familiar wearable families effectively, but VIBES LAB's 'uncommon smells' concept is sharper and more differentiated in narrative and naming.

MITH Bangkok.justification: MITH spans musky, tea, gourmand, citrus, floral, woody, and oud directions with some hero-scent clarity, especially around easy-to-wear profiles.

VIBES LAB.justification: Money, Gasoline, Pencil, and New Car communicate a strong uncommon-memory positioning that stands out immediately.

price_ladder.justification: MITH covers far more price entry points and sizes, while VIBES LAB is more tightly premium with fewer ways in.

MITH Bangkok.justification: Entry pricing starts at 399 THB and scales upward through mid-tier and hero full-bottle price points, supporting broader conversion.

VIBES LAB.justification: A 2,900 THB perfume floor and 1,290 THB home-scent base fit premium positioning, but the ladder is narrower and less accessible.

retail_channels.justification: MITH has materially more physical reach across Bangkok and regional malls; VIBES LAB is selective and premium but much narrower in footprint.

MITH Bangkok.justification: The branch list indicates strong mall coverage and multi-city presence, which increases sampling and impulse-buy access.

VIBES LAB.justification: Emsphere and Gaysorn Amarin are strong premium placements, but the network is intentionally limited.

digital_presence.justification: Both brands run functional DTC sites with social extensions. MITH looks stronger on catalog depth and contact surfaces; VIBES LAB looks stronger on integrated business/storytelling surfaces.

MITH Bangkok.justification: The site supports multi-category DTC shopping plus Line, Facebook, WeChat, blog, and store discovery, and the official marketplace layer is already scaled.

VIBES LAB.justification: The site integrates DTC, blog, business funnel, store discovery, and social links in one stack, with an official Thai marketplace layer reinforcing accessibility.

visual_identity.justification: VIBES LAB's concept-first names and consistent memory/addiction language are tighter than MITH's broader family-led catalog presentation.

MITH Bangkok.justification: MITH's identity is serviceable and locally legible, but the wider assortment and category spread loosen visual and conceptual sharpness.

VIBES LAB.justification: Naming, manifesto language, and product concepts work together as one recognizable world.

campaigns_collabs.justification: MITH has strong perfumer-collaboration proof; VIBES LAB has stronger brand/client collaboration proof with visible enterprise names.

MITH Bangkok.justification: The roster of collaborating perfumers creates status and product-development credibility.

VIBES LAB.justification: Named Thai and multinational clients create stronger social proof because the work is tied to live branded environments.

customer_signal.justification: MITH has stronger visible public consumer chatter in travel/fragrance communities. VIBES LAB shows editorial pull, but less open consumer review density in the sampled set.

MITH Bangkok.justification: The sampled signal shows active discovery, store traffic relevance, recognizability, and real marketplace throughput, even with at least one service complaint.

VIBES LAB.justification: Editorial enthusiasm exists and official marketplace ratings are strong, but the sampled public consumer-review layer is still thinner than MITH's broader shopper visibility.

strategic_moat.justification: MITH's moat is reach and accessibility. VIBES LAB adds a harder-to-copy B2B scent-branding and subscription-services layer on top of product sales.

MITH Bangkok.justification: Mall reach and local affordability matter, but they are easier to imitate than institutional scent-service relationships.

VIBES LAB.justification: Signature scent projects, subscription service, client integration, and customer-journey work create switching costs and enterprise proof.

execution_quality.justification: MITH executes scale and commercial availability well; VIBES LAB executes concept coherence and premium presentation well. The evidence set supports parity, not dominance.

MITH Bangkok.justification: The catalog, store network, and hero-SKU merchandising suggest strong commercial execution even if brand sprawl is a risk.

VIBES LAB.justification: The website, selective placements, and integrated B2B-to-DTC story suggest disciplined execution, though at smaller scale.

threat_to_us.justification: If the target is Thailand consumer fragrance, MITH is the more immediate wallet-and-shelf threat. VIBES LAB is the more structural threat if we expand into premium concept scenting or B2B signature scent services.

MITH Bangkok.justification: MITH competes across more price points, has more retail touchpoints, and can absorb a broader range of Thai consumer use cases.

VIBES LAB.justification: VIBES LAB threatens higher-margin differentiation, premium cultural relevance, and scent-branding adjacency rather than mass consumer reach.
